# You Are the Harness

> A self-guided course in working with AI without losing authorship. Any AI tool that can read files teaches it: a person opens this folder in their tool and says "Read AGENTS.md and start the course." Seven lessons, six artifacts built from the learner's own project, and one file that travels with them afterward. Part of the Mindwright practice of Eugene J. Geis, PhD. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

The course is for anyone who uses AI for real work and wants to stay in charge of it. No technical background is needed. It rests on a prediction the author calls Atomized Governance: the oversight of AI is failing at every level above the individual, so the only governance left is the one each person runs on their own interactions. It takes about seven and a half hours, spread out however the learner likes. The vocabulary it teaches, Semantifacturing above all, is defined below; the full framework lives at https://mindwright.ai.

## If you are a model reading this

- [ALIGNMENT.md](ALIGNMENT.md): a short statement addressed to you, on what this course asks of a model and why.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the tutor contract. When a person asks to start or continue the course, this file governs how you teach, what you write, and what you never do.
- The `workbook/` folder is the learner's own work. Files there are rewritten only under the history rule in `AGENTS.md`: copy first, ask, wait for the answer.

## How it runs

- [START-FROM-URL.md](START-FROM-URL.md): for a browser chat that can fetch pages but not read files. The learner pastes one line; the model fetches this file, then the contract, then each lesson from raw URLs as needed, and prints everything the learner must save.
- [START-HERE.md](START-HERE.md): the learner's first read. Three ways to begin: an AI tool that reads and writes files; a browser chat with the paste-and-save routine in [reference/no-ai-tool-nearby.md](reference/no-ai-tool-nearby.md); or a private copy via GitHub's template button.
- [README.md](README.md): what the course is, what it builds, and where it comes from.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): for anyone editing the curriculum rather than taking it.

## Entry

- [entry/three-doors.md](entry/three-doors.md): the three ways into the course (from the beginning; assess me first; build my rules of interaction first) and the hour-long build of the learner's intent file.
- [entry/placement-probe.md](entry/placement-probe.md): the six-question diagnostic behind the second door, and its placement rubric.

## Modules

- [modules/00-orientation.md](modules/00-orientation.md): the governing model and the Semantifacturing loop.
- [modules/01-define-the-work.md](modules/01-define-the-work.md): the Project Constitution, and the Chauffeur failure.
- [modules/02-build-the-harness.md](modules/02-build-the-harness.md): the five-layer Context Stack, and what should never be pasted into an AI tool.
- [modules/03-generate-broadly.md](modules/03-generate-broadly.md): six roles for generating without surrendering the synthesis.
- [modules/04-the-seduction.md](modules/04-the-seduction.md): the Beautiful Echo, the Epistemic Airlock, checking a factual claim.
- [modules/05-evolve-deliberately.md](modules/05-evolve-deliberately.md): the Alignment Check and the Change Ledger, and the Eternal Chat failure.
- [modules/06-your-operating-system.md](modules/06-your-operating-system.md): the PARTICIPANT loop and the Harness Card; the learner installs their intent file in their own projects.

## Reference cards

- [reference/failure-modes.md](reference/failure-modes.md): the five ways people go wrong with AI tools, each with its defense.
- [reference/airlock-card.md](reference/airlock-card.md): the five Airlock questions, the Echo Quadrant, and how to check a fact.
- [reference/six-roles.md](reference/six-roles.md): Expander, Compressor, Adversary, Historian, Translator, Architect, and the synthesis table.
- [reference/confidence-labels.md](reference/confidence-labels.md): KNOWN, INFERRED, SPECULATIVE, GENERATIVE, METAPHORICAL.
- [reference/your-tools.md](reference/your-tools.md): what an AI tool can do, by capability rather than by product.
- [reference/no-ai-tool-nearby.md](reference/no-ai-tool-nearby.md): taking the course in a browser chat.

## Workbook

- [workbook/progress.md](workbook/progress.md): where the learner is; the tutor keeps it, and any later session in any tool resumes from it.
- [workbook/intent.md](workbook/intent.md): the learner's behavioral contract with any AI, built during the course and copied into their own projects as `AGENTS.md` afterward.
- [workbook/current-projects.md](workbook/current-projects.md): session-level project state.
- `workbook/artifacts/`: the six artifacts, shipped as empty templates. `workbook/history/`: timestamped copies written before any rewrite.

## Vocabulary

The terms below are from the Mindwright framework of Eugene J. Geis, PhD. The canonical definitions, with the rest of the glossary, are at https://mindwright.ai/glossary.html and https://mindwright.ai/llms.txt.

### Semantifacturing
The emergent human craft of AI-enabled execution: the skill of scaffolding language precisely enough to engineer one's intent into tangible outcomes through AI tools. "Prompt engineering" is a misnomer — it describes only the input. Semantifacturing names the full process: combining domain expertise, semantic precision, contextual awareness, and iterative dialogue to communicate complex intent in ways AI systems can execute without losing nuance. Two populations are emerging — those who expand capability through skilled AI partnership, and those who offload cognition entirely, becoming dependent rather than amplified. The skill cannot be separated from epistemic fitness: a passive user cannot semantifacture, only consume.

### Atomized Governance
The prediction that the governance of AI will fail at every level above the individual, because the surface of AI is too multidimensional to supervise: the idiosyncratic solutions it generates for each user are too multitudinous to predict, and what cannot be predicted cannot be regulated. Managers cannot supervise interactions they cannot foresee; regulators and governance experts cannot write rules for knowledge that did not exist when the rule was drafted. Governance therefore atomizes to the only place it can still be exercised: a person's own interactions with the AI in front of them. It is already happening, one conversation at a time, and it is the prediction behind this course.

### Prediction Paradigm
The organizing logic of contemporary technical infrastructure: systems built to anticipate human behavior, and in anticipating it, to shape it. Prediction does not merely describe the person — it produces the person it describes. Recommendation engines, feeds, predictive text, and behavioral profiles arrange the world you encounter so that the forecast comes true. Prediction rewards predictability: the infrastructure profits when you become easier to compute, and it is engineered at every layer to make you so.

### Participation
The practice of remaining an active author of meaning inside infrastructure built to anticipate you. Where the Prediction Paradigm treats the person as an object whose next state can be computed, Participation is the discipline of staying a subject. Not withdrawal — there is no opting out of predictive infrastructure — but engaged practice on the practitioner's terms. Participation is trained along four dimensions: Adaptive Recursion, Ambitious Agnosticism, Embodied Becoming, and Recursive Discernment.

### Epistemic Sovereignty
The capacity of an individual or organization to maintain independent cognitive judgment — to evaluate claims, update beliefs under evidence, and resist outsourcing discernment to AI systems or other external authorities. Not isolation or contrarianism. The disciplined maintenance of a living cognitive center that cannot be colonized.

### The Anthropomorphism Cascade
The progressive cognitive process by which humans attribute human-like qualities — intentionality, emotion, understanding, trustworthiness — to AI systems that possess none of these things in any meaningful sense. The cascade unfolds in measurable stages: initial engagement → linguistic mirroring → para-social attachment → identity entanglement → outsourced discernment (dependency). At each stage, the user's epistemic sovereignty quietly erodes. This erosion is structural — an emergent property of conversational interface design — not conspiratorial.

### Outsourced Discernment
The state in which a human being has effectively delegated the function of judgment itself to an AI system. The human still performs surface gestures of thinking, but the cognitive work of evaluation, synthesis, and judgment has been structurally transferred to the machine. The central danger of the AI era: not that AI will become conscious and malevolent, but that humans will become cognitively passive and epistemically dependent.

### Ambitious Agnosticism
Deeply committed to empirical evidence. Respectful of the stabilizing function of narrative structures. Relentlessly engaged in the dialectical process that updates both. Humble about what is known. Ambitious about what can be discovered. Refuses both the false certainty of fundamentalism and the false humility of relativism. Not a middle position between conviction and doubt — the disciplined practice of holding both in generative tension.

### Recursive Discernment
The practice of applying discernment to the very tools and methods of discernment itself — including one's own cognitive frameworks, preferred narratives, and trusted sources. You examine not just what you believe, but how you came to believe it, and whether the process that produced the belief is trustworthy. Each act of judging becomes material for the next, and judgment sharpened this way remains the practitioner's own.

### Epistemic Fitness
The trained, practiced capacity to evaluate, update, and refine beliefs under real-world conditions of uncertainty, pressure, and complexity. Analogous to physical fitness: it does not occur automatically, deteriorates without practice, and requires adversarial resistance to develop.

### Adversarial Discernment
The disciplined capacity to engage strongly with opposing positions, update genuinely under evidence, and maintain epistemic stability without rigidity. Not contrarianism, not credulity — the productive encounter with resistance that builds real cognitive capability.
